title: Adaptive sparkline density and column compression mode (prototype)
creator: Asha Gupta
description: Prototype an adaptive table density mode that blends compact row layouts with inline sparkline microcharts and a reversible column compression mode. Goal is to reduce vertical space for high-cardinality datasets while preserving key signals (trend sparklines, sort/filter affordances, and accessible keyboard navigation). This ticket covers design exploration, prototype Figma frames, developer handoff tokens, and a lightweight usability test with 6 internal reviewers.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype frames in Figma demonstrating: default/compact/compact+sparkline states and compressed column state
Interaction spec for entering/exiting compression mode (keyboard + mouse + persisted preference)
Design tokens mapped for spacing, typography, and sparkline mini-chart colors; tokens named to align with core theme tokens
Accessibility checklist passed: tab order preserved, aria-labels for compressed cells, contrast for sparkline strokes
Developer-ready component spec including prop surface for: density, sparkline-on/off, compression-threshold, accessible-label-fn
Lightweight usability feedback notes captured and follow-up tickets created for prioritized engineering work
comments: 2026-02-25 - Asha Gupta: Kickoff - sketched three concepts: 'compact rows with sparklines', 'column compression overlay', and 'density toggle with auto-threshold'. Prioritized sparklines + reversible compression for prototype.
2026-03-01 - Lucas Herrera: Created first Figma frames and shared with PM and Eng. Noted trade-off: sparklines require per-row render budget — recommended sampling strategy for large pages.

2026-03-03 - Jonah Kim (Eng): Reviewed prototype. Raised performance concern about server-side sparkline SVG generation for paginated APIs. Suggested client-caching and precomputed mini-series hashes.

2026-03-04 - Design review: Agreed to limit live sparklines to visible viewport rows and provide a low-fidelity shimmer for offscreen rows. Decided compression mode will collapse less important columns to an iconified summary instead of removing them.

2026-03-06 - Accessibility review (Priya Shah): Recommended explicit aria-expanded semantics for compressed columns, focus management when toggling, and text fallback summarization for screen readers.

2026-03-08 - Lucas Herrera: Hand-off version 1 tokens branch created; linked PR and token mapping attached. Engineering to experiment with lazy-sparkline rendering and Preference API for persisted density.

2026-03-10 - Usability run: 6 reviewers (2 PMs, 2 Engs, 2 CSMs). Key findings: compression mode improved glanceability on 40+ column datasets, but discoverability needed a subtle persistent affordance in header. Follow-up ticket created for header affordance and tooltip wording.
notes: Trade-offs: we prefer reversible compression that keeps data discoverable over automatic column hiding. Performance mitigation strategy: viewport-gated rendering + server-side precomputed mini-series for heavy datasets. Will propose a telemetry metric to measure sparkline render cost and visibility.
